newsitem.title: UK: No relief for platinum, palladium market tensions.
newsitem.headline: No relief for platinum, palladium market tensions.

text.p: Prices of the rare precious metals platinum and palladium remained at dizzy heights on Friday with no signs that market tensions would ease in the near future.
"There is not much likelihood of things will change until Russia starts to deliver," one dealer said.
Talks between Russian export officials and Japanese trading houses -- their largest customers for palladium - began this week on agreeing long delayed contracts for 1997 shipments.
Platinum fixed at $497.00 per ounce its highst level since August 23, 1990 and palladium was valued at $240.00, its highest price since March 1980.
Russian is the largest exporter of palladium.

Sources close to Japanese business here said the Russia material was likely to arrive in Japan in July. Russian officials at the negotiations had said they would begin shipments on June 20 having last exported in December.
Barry Davison managing director of South Africa's Amplats, the world's leading producer of platinum, told Reuters the South African producers did not have stocks to ship to the market.

"I don't believe the South Afircan primary producers have stocks of metal. I don't think relief can come from here. The relief can only come from a resumption of Russian supplies and dishoarding of the metal," he said in an interview.
German catalytic converter maker Degussa AG could face production curbs if the current supply squeeze on the platinum market continues for another three to four weeks, a company official said.
"That is the warning flag we are raising," Ralf Drieselmann, head of precious metals trading, told Reuters.
Degussa produces 15 to 25 percent of the world's catalytic converters, which filter harmful gases from auto exhaust fumes.
A meeting of the London Platinum and Palladium Market Association late on Thursday confirmed that there had been no delivery defaults in the market.
However market sources said that could change if the liquidity squeeze continued.
"The Russians could do spot deals into Zurich (the contractual delivery point for platinum and palladium deals) and that would help to alleviate the situation," a dealer said.
He added there was no indication that was forthcoming.

The only other sources of metal would be sales from the U.S. strategic stockpile or positions on the Nymex and Tocom (Tokyo Commodity Exchange) futures markets being unwound, both of which were unlikely, dealers said.
"As we get further into June, we could see a lot more activity," one dealer warned.
Gold and silver prices were both a little firmer on the back of platinum and palladium. Gold fixed at $344.00 upfrom $340.80 on Thursday and silver was at $4.88/$4.91, up nine cents.
